metadata.title: Multi-Dimensional OKR Alignment Scoring System
metadata.title_zh: 多維度 OKR 對齊評分系統
metadata.priority_date: To be established upon provisional filing

abstract.en: A computer-implemented method for evaluating alignment of goal statements within a hierarchical organisation using three independent scoring dimensions. The method computes a strategic alignment score by comparing goal statements against scope-weighted strategy documents, a vertical alignment score by traversing management hierarchies to find parent objectives, and a quality alignment score by evaluating adherence to goal-setting methodology. A composite score is calculated as a weighted combination with proportional normalisation when dimensions are unavailable, providing a transparent per-dimension breakdown with actionable improvement suggestions.
abstract.zh_tw: 一種用於評估階層式組織內目標陳述對齊程度的電腦實施方法，採用三個獨立評分維度。該方法透過將目標陳述與範圍加權之策略文件進行比較來計算策略對齊分數，透過遍歷管理階層以尋找上級目標來計算垂直對齊分數，以及透過評估是否符合目標設定方法論來計算品質對齊分數。以加權組合計算複合分數，當維度不可用時進行比例正規化，提供透明的各維度分數分解及可操作的改善建議。

background: Enterprise goal management systems require employees to create Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) that align with organisational strategy. Existing systems evaluate alignment using simplistic approaches: keyword matching between child and parent goals, or single-dimensional similarity scoring. These approaches fail to capture the multi-faceted nature of organisational alignment.

In real organisations, an objective must simultaneously align with (a) strategic direction documents at varying organisational levels, (b) direct supervisor or parent objectives in the management hierarchy, and (c) established goal-setting methodology. Existing systems treat these as a single alignment check, producing scores that are neither transparent nor actionable.

Furthermore, organisations have hierarchical structures where team-level strategy is more relevant than company-wide strategy for individual contributors. Existing RAG systems retrieve documents without awareness of organisational proximity, weighting all documents equally regardless of their scope relationship to the user.

overview: The disclosed method evaluates goal alignment across three independent scoring dimensions: Strategic Alignment, Vertical Alignment, and Quality Alignment. Each dimension is computed independently using embedding-based semantic similarity, then combined using a configurable weighted formula with proportional normalisation when dimensions are unavailable.

The system introduces scope-aware document weighting that adjusts retrieval relevance based on organisational proximity (team documents weighted 1.2x, department 1.0x, company 0.8x). It further implements dynamic management chain traversal that searches up to three levels of the organisational hierarchy to find approved parent objectives when the direct supervisor has none.

The result is a composite alignment score (0–100) with a transparent per-dimension breakdown, warnings for low-scoring dimensions, and actionable suggestions for improvement. The system supports bilingual evaluation in English and Chinese.
key_innovations: Scope-aware document weighting based on organisational proximity
Dynamic management chain traversal with circular reference detection
Proportional weight normalisation when dimensions unavailable
Bilingual support with CJK character detection

detailed_description.system_architecture: The alignment scoring system comprises three independent scoring engines, a composite calculator, and a scope-aware context retrieval module. The system receives as input an OKR (objective description plus key results), the user's organisational context (team, department, supervisor chain), and pre-embedded strategy documents stored in a vector database (pgvector).

components.name: Strategic Alignment
components.description: Measures how well an OKR aligns with organisational strategy documents. The system retrieves relevant documents from a vector database using the OKR text as a query, then applies scope-aware weighting.

sub_components.name: OKR Reference Materials
sub_components.description: Playbooks and methodology books receive priority weight of 1.1x as primary grounding sources

components.name: Vertical Alignment
components.description: Measures how well an OKR connects to its parent objective or supervisor's approved objectives in the organisational hierarchy.

sub_components.name: Step 1: Parent Objective
sub_components.description: If the OKR has a designated parent objective, compute cosine similarity between the child OKR embedding and the parent OKR embedding (including key results).

sub_components.name: Step 2: Supervisor's Objectives
sub_components.description: If no parent is designated, retrieve the direct supervisor's APPROVED objectives and compute similarity against each, selecting the best match.

sub_components.name: Step 3: Management Chain Traversal
sub_components.description: If the direct supervisor has no approved objectives, traverse up the management chain (maximum 3 levels) with circular reference detection, searching each level for approved objectives.

components.name: Quality Alignment
components.description: Measures adherence to OKR methodology best practices.

sub_components.name: Measurability
sub_components.description: Whether key results contain quantitative targets. Detection uses regex patterns for percentages, counts, currency, ranges, and metric acronyms (NPS, CSAT, ROI). Chinese patterns detect measure words and Chinese numerals. A threshold of 50% measurable KRs flags the OKR as having measurable key results, adding a 10-point bonus.

sub_components.name: OKR Structure
sub_components.description: Whether the objective has at least 2 key results, adding a 5-point bonus.

sub_components.name: Methodology Grounding
sub_components.description: Semantic similarity against OKR reference materials (top_k=5 from vector database) forms the base quality score.

components.name: Composite Score Calculation
components.description: The composite score is calculated using configurable weights that sum to 1.0. When one or more dimensions are unavailable (e.g., no strategy documents uploaded), the weights are normalised proportionally.

variables.available_weights: Sum of weights for available dimensions

bilingual_support.detection_method: CJK Unified Ideograph character frequency (threshold: >30% of non-whitespace characters)

claims.text: A computer-implemented method for evaluating alignment of a goal statement within a hierarchical organisation, the method comprising: (a) computing a first alignment score by comparing the goal statement against strategy documents using embedding-based semantic similarity, wherein the strategy documents are weighted based on organisational scope proximity to the user, with team-scope documents receiving a higher weight than department-scope documents, and department-scope documents receiving a higher weight than company-scope documents; (b) computing a second alignment score by comparing the goal statement against parent objectives in a management hierarchy, including dynamically traversing up to N levels of the management chain when no direct parent objective is available; (c) computing a third alignment score by evaluating the goal statement against methodology best practices, including measuring quantifiability of associated key results; and (d) computing a composite alignment score as a weighted combination of the first, second, and third alignment scores, with proportional weight normalisation when one or more dimensions are unavailable.

The method of claim 1, wherein the scope-based weighting comprises multiplying similarity scores by a team weight of 1.2, a department weight of 1.0, and a company weight of 0.8, with the weighted score capped at a maximum of 100.
The method of claim 1, wherein the dynamic management chain traversal includes circular reference detection to prevent infinite traversal loops in organisational hierarchies.

The method of claim 1, wherein the measurability evaluation uses language-specific regex patterns to detect quantitative targets in both English and Chinese character sets, with a Chinese character detection threshold of 30% of non-whitespace characters.
The method of claim 1, further comprising an embedding cache using least-recently-used eviction to avoid redundant vector database queries during batch alignment recalculation.

The method of claim 1, wherein the composite alignment score is returned as a structured breakdown comprising per-dimension scores, the calculation method used, warnings for low-scoring dimensions, and actionable suggestions for improvement.

reviewed_systems.name: WorkBoard, Tability, Weekdone
reviewed_systems.description: Commercial OKR platforms offer AI-assisted alignment suggestions
reviewed_systems.limitation: Use single-dimensional similarity (parent-child matching only). None publish multi-dimensional composite scoring with scope weighting.

reviewed_systems.name: Standard RAG systems (LangChain, LlamaIndex)
reviewed_systems.limitation: No organisational scope awareness. Documents are treated equally regardless of their relationship to the user's position in the hierarchy.

prior_art.differentiation: The combination of three independent scoring dimensions, scope-weighted retrieval, dynamic hierarchy traversal, and proportional weight normalisation constitutes a non-obvious improvement over existing goal alignment systems.
